title: Effects of equine-assisted therapy on transdiagnostic consequences of aversive childhood experiences
summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of an equine-assisted group therapy (PGT) compared to s behavioral activation group therapy (BA) in patients with aversive childhood experiences in an acute psychiatric setting. Groups will be formed with four patients each, who will participate in either the six-week PGT or the six-week BA (control group). We expect that the PGT will significantly improve the self-efficacy of the participating patients compared to the control group. In addition, we are using a semi-structured interview to investigate how PGT affects treatment satisfaction.
conditions: All patients aged 18-60 years with aversive childhood experiences, measured by CTQ (F3x, F4x, F5x, F6x). Exclusion criteria are organic, including symptomatic mental disorders (F00-F09), autism (F84), schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders (F20-F29) and substance and alcohol abuse in the last 2 weeks

interventions.name: Equine-assisted intervention with two Shetland Ponys (6 sessions of 60 minutes over 6 weeks, group size: 4 participants)
Active control group: Behavioral Activation (6 sessions of 60 minutes over 6 weeks, group size: 4 participants)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients aged 18-60 years with aversive childhood experiences, measured by CTQ (subscales: emotional abuse, physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional neglect and physical neglect); Severity: min. “moderate to severe” on one of the subscales
Exclusion criteria:
● Acute suicidal tendencies
● Organic, including symptomatic mental disorders (F00-F09)
● Substance and alcohol abuse in the last 2 weeks
● Autism (F84)
● Schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders (F20-F29)
● Placement according to PsychKG
● Pregnancy
● Epilepsy (G40)
● Immobility (R26)
● Horse hair allergy
